issue.title: Host reboot leaves GPU containers with stale CUDA context (silent outage)
issue.symptom:
2026-10-12 host reboot (~7.6h uptime at discovery) left gaia-core, gaia-audio, gaia-prime (and gaia-core-candidate) all started at the same instant (16:42:33) with a broken CUDA driver-API context: nvidia-smi inside each container worked fine, but torch.cuda.is_available() raised 'CUDA unknown error... Setting the available devices to be zero.' Docker health checks reported all these containers as healthy throughout, because health checks don't exercise CUDA. The outage was completely silent until the user tried to chat in the dashboard and gaia-core's embedded engine crashed on the Neural Handoff prefix-cache's tokenizer .to(device) call (gaia-engine/gaia_engine/core.py PrefixCache.get_kv(), ~line 491), which took down every /v1/chat/completions call (worker 500 -> engine-manager proxy 502), and the Groq cloud fallback was also broken (see linked issue), so the chat request had nowhere to fall back to and errored with GAIA-CORE-078.

Fix applied tonight: docker compose restart on gaia-core, gaia-audio, gaia-prime, and (via -f docker-compose.candidate.yml) gaia-core-candidate. All four now report torch.cuda.is_available()==True and chat works end-to-end again.

Follow-up needed: (1) a startup/health check that actually exercises CUDA (e.g. torch.cuda.is_available() or a trivial tensor .to('cuda') op) should be added to gaia-doctor's health polling or each service's own /health, so this class of failure surfaces immediately instead of silently waiting for a user-facing crash. (2) Consider whether docker-compose restart policy / systemd unit ordering should wait for nvidia-persistenced or a GPU-ready signal before GPU-touching containers start on boot, to prevent the race in the first place.

# candidates/gaia-core/tests/test_observer_health_endpoint.py
"""Tests for the /health endpoint regarding Observer health."""

import pytest
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import gaia_core.main as main_mod


@pytest.fixture


def test_health_endpoint_degrades_on_embedded_engine_cuda_unhealthy(client):
    """GAIA_Project-t0f2: the embedded engine's own /health now reports
    cuda_healthy=False when it expects GPU but CUDA is dead (stale driver
    context after a host reboot). gaia-core's /health must surface that as
    degraded too, the same way an engine drain already does -- this is what
    lets Doctor's existing status=="degraded" remediation pick it up
    without any Doctor-side changes."""
    with (
        patch("httpx.AsyncClient") as mock_async_client_cls,
        patch("gaia_core.utils.stream_observer.observer_health") as mock_obs_health,
    ):
        mock_client = MagicMock()
        mock_resp = MagicMock()
        mock_resp.status_code = 200
        mock_resp.json.return_value = {
            "cuda_healthy": False,
            "cuda_detail": "device='cuda' but torch.cuda.is_available() is False",
        }

        async def mock_get(*args, **kwargs):
            return mock_resp

        mock_client.get = mock_get

        async def __aenter__(self):
            return mock_client

        async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
            pass

        mock_async_client_cls.return_value.__aenter__ = __aenter__
        mock_async_client_cls.return_value.__aexit__ = __aexit__

        mock_obs_health.return_value = {
            "observations": 10, "failures": 1, "fail_rate": 0.1, "healthy": True,
        }

        with patch("time.monotonic", return_value=main_mod._core_boot_time + 200):
            resp = client.get("/health")

        assert resp.status_code == 200
        data = resp.json()
        assert data["status"] == "degraded"
        assert data["inference_ok"] is False
        assert "cuda" in data["inference_detail"].lower()


def test_health_endpoint_stays_healthy_when_cuda_healthy_true(client):
    """A normal, healthy embedded-engine response (cuda_healthy=True, or
    device=cpu so the field is absent entirely) must not spuriously degrade."""
    with (
        patch("httpx.AsyncClient") as mock_async_client_cls,
        patch("gaia_core.utils.stream_observer.observer_health") as mock_obs_health,
    ):
        mock_client = MagicMock()
        mock_resp = MagicMock()
        mock_resp.status_code = 200
        mock_resp.json.return_value = {"cuda_healthy": True, "cuda_detail": "cuda available"}

        async def mock_get(*args, **kwargs):
            return mock_resp

        mock_client.get = mock_get

        async def __aenter__(self):
            return mock_client

        async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
            pass

        mock_async_client_cls.return_value.__aenter__ = __aenter__
        mock_async_client_cls.return_value.__aexit__ = __aexit__

        mock_obs_health.return_value = {
            "observations": 10, "failures": 1, "fail_rate": 0.1, "healthy": True,
        }

        with patch("time.monotonic", return_value=main_mod._core_boot_time + 200):
            resp = client.get("/health")

        assert resp.status_code == 200
        data = resp.json()
        assert data["status"] == "healthy"
